_schema.applies_to: matcher on {program, metrics, subgroups}; null = any
_schema.basis: traceability: the country report's own notes and health warnings, a GitHub issue, or a measured diagnostic in this repo's data

annotations.text: UKMOD 'ukmod'-variant rows are simulated statistics from a peer FRS-based microsimulation, not measurements: same survey base as PE UK but different weighting (HBAI-adjusted FRS 2023/24), different uprating, and take-up corrections frozen at 2021 outside Scotland/pension-age (the report's own health warning). PE-vs-UKMOD divergence decomposes into data-vintage, uprating, take-up and policy-scope channels before it says anything about either engine.

'official_as_cited' rows are the report's transcription of DWP/HMRC/OBR/SFC estimates, kept here to reproduce UKMOD's own validation frame. Before scoring PE against those values, resolve them to the primary publication (several are already ingested lanes: HMRC liabilities, OBR EFO March 2026) — cite the primary, and treat any transcription mismatch as an external-issue seed against this report.

Caseloads count families except where the report marks (c) children, (h) households, (i) individuals — carried per row as unit_concept. Child Benefit appears twice (families and children covered); Income Support includes income-based JSA. Match the unit before comparing.

Periods are UKMOD policy years (the system as at a reference date in the named calendar year), not DWP/HMRC financial years; forecasts start in 2025. A PE counterpart should simulate the matching policy year, and comparisons to FY-denominated official statistics inherit a timing wedge.

Distribution and poverty statistics are before-housing-costs household equivalised disposable income, modified OECD scale, individual unit of analysis — the same construction as the hbai-poverty lane's BHC rows, so the three-way PE/UKMOD/HBAI triangle is well-posed on this definition. The report itself flags UKMOD child poverty understating HBAI, attributing it to child-benefit take-up assumptions.
Gini, quintile shares and poverty rates are printed to whole percents (fractions carry ±0.005); caseloads to thousands; expenditure to £ millions. Score within rounding tolerance.

UKMOD is open source, so confirmed external-model issues here have an upstream path (unique among UK lanes). Case-level adjudication belongs to the mode-3 ukmod-cases lane via the JRC connector (#41); this lane stays at published-aggregate altitude.
